clue.text: Air force officer's good, playing part in a coup

indicators.note: actors playing a part reshape it, so the words that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An RAF officer, a decent sort, has taken a role in a military takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition carries 's for 'is': the officer IS the wordplay that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A group captain is a senior commissioned rank in the Royal Air Force, equal to a naval captain.

clue.text: Flickering fire, ample guide for climbers?

indicators.note: something flickering keeps shifting and moving, so the following letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A generous campfire flickers beside a trail guide for mountaineers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: a map showing hills in raised form would help mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief map shows height and terrain contours, the sort of chart useful to people scaling mountains.

clue.text: Section of account I led up to

indicators.note: a section is a piece cut from within the following phrase, so the letters lie inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the word boundaries of this phrase

explanation.surface: Someone describes their part in a story they led up to.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are prepositions of time meaning as far as a stated point, as in 'wait till noon'.

clue.text: Actor not bothered about line in singing voice

indicators.note: someone bothered is flustered and disturbed, so these letters get thrown about
about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters wrap round the next item

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
L is the usual abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A careless performer can't be bothered to learn a line of the song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor not bothered' reads as an indifferent performer, but 'bothered' works on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female vocal range, so it names a kind of singing voice.

clue.text: Fruit, soft and fleshy

blocks.note: a plum is a stone fruit
p is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A description of ripe fruit, soft to the touch and full of flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and fleshy are near synonyms, both describing a body or object that is pleasantly rounded and full.

clue.text: Nice tip perhaps designed for training period

indicators.note: something designed has been worked out and arranged afresh, so the fodder is reordered

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A useful hint has been crafted to help with a course of instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' looks like a hedge on the tip but is fodder, its letters all needed.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprenticeship is the fixed term a learner spends being taught a trade by a skilled worker.

clue.text: Open, reserving right to be annoyed

indicators.note: to reserve something is to hold it, so the first word keeps the next item inside

blocks.note: naked means open, as in naked aggression or exposed to view
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone who is candid but keeps the right to be irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: Narked is British slang for irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: Narked is informal British slang for irritated or put out, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Grant agreement

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to give or bestow, as in to bestow honours
second meaning: a noun, a pact or harmony between parties

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a funding agreement, but the two words are separate meanings, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to bestow something on someone and a formal settlement reached between two sides.

clue.text: Film director's treatment of senator's crimes

indicators.note: a treatment works material over and reshapes it, so the following letters are remade

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter including the S

explanation.surface: A film-maker's screen treatment of a politician's misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treatment' is a real film term for a script outline, which makes the surface convincing; here the 's after director stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American who made Taxi Driver, Goodfellas and The Departed.

clue.text: US city in plan linked to a new fraud

indicators.note: in means the city sits inside the word for plan

blocks.note: a chart is a plan or map
LA is Los Angeles
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An American city's scheme turns out to be tied to a fresh swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A charlatan is a person falsely claiming skill or knowledge, so a fraud in the sense of an impostor.

clue.text: Superior meal, not small

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the item that follows from the meal

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A refined dinner that is generous in portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper and superior both mean higher in rank or position, as in the upper classes.

clue.text: Old, spoilt meat, large area turning greyish-yellow

indicators.note: spoilt food has gone off and been ruined, so its letters are scrambled
turning round means the last two abbreviations are read backwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the fodder, taken as written
L is the abbreviation for large
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Stale old meat going a sickly yellowish-grey colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is the name of a pale greyish-fawn shade, after the colour of ground oats.

clue.text: Drama company with rented theatre finally full

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: rep is short for a repertory theatre company
a let property is one rented out
the last letter of theatre

explanation.surface: A touring troupe hires a theatre and at last plays to a full house.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete means filled to capacity or well supplied, often after a large meal.

clue.text: Material, extracted, put about

indicators.note: put about is a sailing term for turning round, so the word heads back the other way

blocks.note: mined means dug out, extracted from the earth

explanation.surface: Some substance has been removed and spread around.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill cloth, the fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Fine time to grab souvenir without resistance

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the item for resistance is dropped
to grab is to seize and hold, so the word for time encloses the other piece

blocks.note: a date is a point in time
a relic is a keepsake or memento
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A good moment to snatch a memento without anyone objecting.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicate and fine both describe something of slender, intricate, easily damaged quality, like fine lace.

clue.text: Dog wagging tail and protecting mother

indicators.note: a wagging tail swings to and fro, so the following letters are jumbled
protecting means shielding, so the shuffled letters surround the next piece

blocks.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A dog wags its tail as it guards its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a link joining the two halves, but its letters are needed in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian is a breed of dog, white with black or liver spots, so it is an example.

clue.text: Opener in county's team

blocks.note: Cork is an Irish county, with the possessive S
a crew is a team, as in a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A sporting opener, like a batsman, playing for a county side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a batsman in a cricket county team; it means a device that opens wine bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew is the spiral tool used to draw corks, so it is something that opens bottles.

clue.text: Article about unusual cupola in Mexican resort

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are not in their normal order

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
c is circa, Latin for about
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A travel piece about a strange domed roof in a Mexican holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a famous beach resort on Mexico's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Go over cornfield initially during harvest

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
during means within the span of, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to reap is to harvest a crop
the first letter of cornfield

explanation.surface: A farmer crosses a cornfield first thing at harvest time.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise or restate, so going over points again is the same idea.

clue.text: Push up in battlefield deployment

indicators.note: in means the letters sit within the phrase that follows
in a down entry up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Troops push up into positions on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: Push here means sell, especially drugs, as a pusher does.
explanation.definitionFit: To push goods, especially illegal drugs, is to peddle them, selling them persistently or illicitly.

clue.text: Commercial full of inspiration entertained

indicators.note: full of means holding inside, so the first word is filled with the second

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
a muse is a source of artistic inspiration

explanation.surface: A creative TV advert that kept viewers diverted.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused and entertained both describe being diverted or made to smile, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Instrument in middle of shrine guarded by snake

indicators.note: middle of keeps only the central letters of the following word
guarded by means surrounded and protected, so the snake encloses the letters

blocks.note: the mamba is a venomous African snake
the middle two letters of shrine

explanation.surface: A sacred object at a temple's centre is watched over by a serpent.
explanation.definitionFit: A marimba is a large wooden percussion instrument, a deep-toned kind of xylophone.

clue.text: Customs further south

blocks.note: more means further or additional
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Traditions found further to the south.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the established conventions and customs of a community, a direct plural synonym.

clue.text: Treated badly, not noticed around university

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the first word wraps the abbreviation

blocks.note: missed means overlooked, not noticed
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student mistreated and overlooked around the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Misused means handled wrongly or abused, a past-tense match for treated badly.

clue.text: Two-wheeled vehicle was miserable

blocks.note: first meaning: a small low-powered motorbike with pedals
second meaning: past tense of a verb for sulking listlessly

explanation.surface: Someone's scooter was in a sorry state, or they were glum about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a light motorcycle, and the verb's past tense means sulked or felt gloomy and listless.

clue.text: Absolute prophet capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means seizing and holding, so the first word encloses the next

blocks.note: a seer is a prophet
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: An all-powerful prophet wins people's hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer and absolute both mean utter or complete, as in sheer nonsense.

clue.text: One with power consumed by warlike objective

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed into, so the letter goes inside the word for warlike

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
martial means relating to war
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A powerful figure swallowed up by an aggressive goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like a noun meaning goal; it is the adjective meaning unbiased.
explanation.definitionFit: Impartial and objective both describe judging fairly, without personal bias or favouritism.

clue.text: Sauce, out of order, bringing reprimand

blocks.note: a dressing is a sauce for salad
a machine that is down is out of action

explanation.surface: A cook's sauce goes wrong and earns a telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing-down is a severe scolding, an idiomatic equivalent of a sharp telling-off.
